flagged_choice_verdicts.quiet=True: ACCEPT (necessary). In pydeseq2 0.5.4, quiet only gates print() calls. summary() prints results_df to stdout, and the size-factor message 'Using None as control genes...' also goes to stdout. test_quiet_and_copy_choices showed non-empty stdout with quiet=False, empty stdout with quiet=True, and bitwise-identical results. The stdio transport test then confirmed every stdout line is JSON-RPC during a DE call.
flagged_choice_verdicts.adata.copy(): ACCEPT (necessary). DeseqDataSet does __dict__.update(adata.__dict__) and adds trend_coeffs and disp_function_type to the caller's uns (re-observed in this session). Copying protects the loaded object. The DE results are bitwise equal to the notebook, and the input .h5ad is unchanged.
flagged_choice_verdicts.float cast in PCA: ACCEPT with corrected rationale. The cast is not needed to avoid a crash: scanpy normalize_total silently converts integer X to float32 (probe_intX.py). The wrapper instead processes integer counts in float64, the dtype of the tutorial's loader (dc.ds.hsctgfb casts with astype(float)). On int64 counts the wrapper equals the direct tutorial calls on X.astype(float64) bitwise, and differs from scanpy's native float32 path by less than 1e-5 in variance ratio. Float inputs are only copied. This is a documented dtype choice, not a scientific change.
flagged_choice_verdicts.dropping swap_layer: ACCEPT. The tool writes no AnnData back, and none of its outputs depend on X after PCA (rank_obsm uses obsm/obs; the plots use obsm/uns/obs columns only, because color_keys must be obs columns). The direct tutorial path including layers['counts'] + dc.pp.swap_layer equals the wrapper bitwise.
flagged_choice_verdicts.CollecTRI dotplot settings: ACCEPT as a documented addition. The scanner's tool specification requires a dot plot for every network. The CollecTRI dot plot uses dc.pl.dotplot with the cell-46 settings: scale 0.15, which is the upstream default, and figsize (4,4). Its data equals the cell-46 transformation applied directly to the reference CollecTRI acts and padj. There is no tutorial figure to compare against; I looked at the image (top 10: SRF, MYOCD, SMAD3, TCF21, ZEB2, SMAD2 / IRF1, SKIL, NR1H4, NR4A3).
flagged_choice_verdicts.leading-edge +/- split on every weighted: ACCEPT. The GSEA running sum in dc.pl.leading_edge ignores weights, so mixing activating and repressing targets would blur the edge. Cell 50 is the tutorial's own remedy, and the scanner specified it for signed networks. It reproduces cells 50 and 60 exactly; for CollecTRI (weights +/-1; 5822 negative edges, no zero weights in either snapshot) it equals direct split calls. Zero-weight edges would be dropped from both parts, as in cell 50. Recorded as an extension beyond the tutorial for CollecTRI.
flagged_choice_verdicts.global plot lock: ACCEPT. FastMCP 4.0.3 runs sync tools in worker threads, and pyplot state is process-global (dc.pl.obsm calls plt.close() on the current figure). Five concurrent calls through one client used 5 worker threads and made 14 plot calls; none overlapped in time, and all results equalled the references. Only plotting is locked, so computation such as DESeq2 still runs concurrently.
flagged_choice_verdicts.sc.set_figure_params at import: ACCEPT for this server, with a caveat. This is tutorial cell 2. It writes nothing to stdout (stdio test), but it changes process-wide rcParams: figure.figsize [6.4,4.8]->[3,3], figure.dpi 100->80, savefig.dpi 'figure'->150, font.size 10->14, axes.grid False->True. If the coordinator mounts other plotting modules in the same process, their figure style changes too. In that case, scope it with plt.rc_context inside _PLOT_LOCK. Not changed here.

changed_input_checks.relabelled_property_threshold_revision: My first secondary threshold (Pearson r of stat > 0.99999, LFC rtol/atol 1e-4) was set before seeing data and failed at r = 0.99990. The primary check (wrapper bitwise equal to a direct call on the same input) was never relaxed. The secondary property now uses LFC, rank and significant-set criteria with margins based on these observations.
